main_text.head: S. P. D.
main_text.p: COgitanti mihi, cuinam hunc ingenii fœtum, jam luci maturum, pro veteri more potissimum offerrem; Ve-ltra, SERENISSIME PRINCEPS, & ILLUSTRES PROCERES, Illustrissima Nomina illico occurrebant, quibus, quicquid hoc est libelli, non tantum honeste posset, sed & summo merito inscribere deberem. Cum enim variæ causæ dari queant, quarum singulæ per se satis graves justæque aliis esse solent, quibus, ut libros suos Viris Principibus sacros faciant, inducantur: tum mihi illas video atque intelligo pene esse universas. Sive enim otii, quod cum ante alibi in Hebræarum literarum studiis, tum hoc proximo triennio in hac alma Academia exegi, ratio mihi sit reddenda; Vobis eam in primis constare debere arbitror, quorum judicio & jussu earundem literarum in Illustri Vestro Athenæo publicam Professionem sustineo. Sive ii, qui
Note: the opening word "Ogitanti" is printed after the woodcut initial C, which forms the first letter of the word "Cogitanti".

page.notes: The first word is a large woodcut initial C joined to "Ogitanti"; the text is transcribed as "Cogitanti" with the initial. The line "Ve-ltra" appears where the printed "Ve-" and "itra" are split by the initial's shadow; "Vestra" is intended. The word "Ve-" beside the initial is partly obscured; "ltra" is probably "stra" and reads as "Vestra" in the print. The catchword "mo" at the lower right is partly cut off. The running head is in spaced capitals and the S. P. D. line is the salutation head. Several words are hard to read in the scan and are marked as uncertain where doubtful.
